reply_text:
Rob's four new commits are merged into `tail-call-depth` (merge commit `a8490b5`) with no conflicts, and none of our work is lost. `startup-linux` is not merged yet because kimi-1 is working in that worktree right now.

I couldn't find a written merge procedure, so this is what I did; say if yours differs:
- **Fetched** `origin`: `a372214..d15de97`, 115 files, about 40,000 added lines. Most of it is morpheus tests and missions, diagnostics, and 15 files under `src/mfuton/lean`.
- **Moved local `main`** to `origin/main`.
- **Merged into `tail-call-depth`.** No file Rob changed is one we changed on either of our branches.
- **Reran the C-authority sweep** after the merge: outcomes are identical to before (202 passed, 54 failed, 3 errors). 53 of 54 files were skipped as current and one was rerun.

Still to do:
- **`startup-linux`:** I'll merge `main` into it when kimi-1's current discovery job returns, so I don't change files under it mid-run.
- **Rob's new tests:** I haven't run the new morpheus and roundtrip tests here. Only the C-authority directory is baselined.
- **Nothing is pushed.** Our three branches (`tail-call-depth`, `nat-natives`, `startup-linux`) and the updated `main` exist only on this machine; the fork on GitHub is still at Rob's old commit. Pushing them to the fork would be the real protection against losing the work. Shall I push all four there?

I've added these steps to the project memory so the next merge follows the same route.
